confirm.title: Add Tensite battery cluster
confirm.description:
Connect through {name} at {address}?

Every battery in a bank advertises separately, so all of them appear here. Connecting through the bank master covers the whole cluster; connecting through another battery is also fine, and is useful for debugging a single unit.

Home Assistant will now connect and check what this battery reports. That can take up to half a minute.

user.title: Add Tensite battery cluster
user.description: Choose the battery to connect through. The bank master relays data for every battery in its cluster; other batteries can also be used, which is useful when debugging one unit.

battery_count.title: Batteries in this cluster
battery_count.description:
The probe heard back from {found} battery/batteries ({serials}).

Nothing in the protocol reports the bank size, and the gateway answers its batteries in rotation, so a single probe can undercount. Confirm the real number: each poll then ends as soon as they have all reported, instead of always waiting out the listening window.

error.cannot_connect: Could not connect. The gateway accepts only one Bluetooth connection at a time, so check nothing else is talking to it — another script, an add-on, or the Tensite app.
error.no_batteries: Connected, but this battery reported no data. It may not be relaying for its cluster. Try the bank master instead.

abort.already_configured: This battery is already set up
abort.no_devices_found: No Tensite batteries found. Check they are powered and in range, and that nothing else is holding the gateway's Bluetooth connection.
abort.not_connectable: This battery was only seen by a non-connectable Bluetooth adapter or proxy. An active connection is required to read cell data.

data_description.scan_interval: How long to wait after one poll finishes before starting the next. It is a delay, not a fixed period: a poll itself takes 4-7 seconds, so a 60 second delay produces a reading roughly every 66 seconds. The battery gateway accepts only one Bluetooth connection at a time, so a short delay will keep the Tensite app from connecting. Below about a minute you are mostly sampling noise, since cell voltages drift by a few millivolts over minutes -- short delays are for watching something happen, not for logging. A new poll never starts while one is still running.
data_description.expected_batteries: How many batteries are in this cluster. Set it and each poll ends as soon as they have all reported, which is much quicker. Left at 0, every poll waits out the full listening window — slower, but it cannot miss a battery that reports late.
data_description.hide_sentinel_temperatures: A pack temperature sensor that is not returning a reading reports -50 °C or -30 °C. By default those values are shown exactly as the Tensite app shows them. Enable this to report those sensors as unavailable instead, so they do not distort temperature history. Only those two values are affected — a genuinely cold pack below freezing is still reported normally.
